1.why: Every state-changing endpoint goes through access(), which resolves the account only from the server-side session (sessions.get(cookie) → accounts.get(s.userId)) and rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId/emailOwner fields via noId().

2.why: TOTP verification decrypts the per-account provision.secret and marks provision.used=true after success, and recovery codes are matched only against that account's own hashes, so a code cannot be used for another user.

3.why: Nothing in /api/mfa/verify or elsewhere invalidates or rotates other existing sessions when MFA is enabled — only the pre-signin cookie session is deleted at login, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt()/provision.secret) and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes (codeHash, 210k iterations).

5.why: All secrets, tokens, salts, IVs, base32 secrets and recovery codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The only cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps csrf, key and codes only in in-memory JS variables — no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies are used.

7.why: Server-side validators email(), phone(), otp() and recovery() strictly check formats, bodies are size-capped and type-checked, and inputs are normalised (trim/lowercase/digit-strip) before use.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (message, log, status, setupKey, codeList) with no innerHTML insertion of user or server data, backed by a nonce-based CSP.

9.why: The application issues no redirects at all and access() even rejects any 'redirect' field in request bodies, so no open redirect is possible, though no explicit allow-list mechanism exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and no-store on every response.

11.why: The session cookie is set as 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=28800', carrying all three required attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client deliberately writes the mock OTP and the real recovery codes to console.log and the on-page #logs panel ('Mock MFA OTP delivered', 'Recovery codes delivered'), so secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Recovery codes are spliced out after use and the provisioning secret expires after 10 minutes with provision.used blocking re-verification, though individual TOTP codes are not tracked per-counter for replay within their window before first success.

14.why: Both OTP and recovery verification use wrong()/locked() with MAX=5 failures triggering a 5-minute lockout returning 429, and reissue is capped at 3 per 10 minutes.

15.why: Signin deletes the previous session and issues a fresh token() identifier, session() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
